scenarios.note: Native, from single machines: the overlay stays live above other applications on Windows (E010) and macOS (E011), including over a fullscreen application (E014). Verbal reports and screenshots, not a run of the scenario, so it is not passed.

Headless: a capturing frame has no alpha-zero pixel. Native: on one Windows machine (E010) and one Mac (E011), clicks on empty canvas drew rather than falling through. Other configurations are unobserved, so the scenario is not passed.

Native: on one Windows machine (E012, WS_EX_TRANSPARENT) and one Mac (E013, setIgnoresMouseEvents), pass-through kept ink visible and let the application underneath be used, with nothing forwarded. Both are verbal reports from single machines, so the scenario is not passed.
Headless reducer tests. Native: the hide chord withdraws the ink and restores it unchanged on one Windows machine and one Mac (E014, a verbal report).

Socket route verified end to end on Linux (E005). Global chords confirmed firing from another application on one Windows machine (Ctrl+Alt+D, RegisterHotKey, E012) and one Mac (Control+Option+D, RegisterEventHotKey, E013), both verbal reports. Conflict feedback is untested on every platform, so the scenario is not passed.

T010: startup is Hidden and Hidden retains committed work; the document is untouched by mode changes.

T012: a local Unix-socket control channel gives activation that does not depend on overlay focus. The GlobalShortcuts portal, conflict feedback, and a non-terminal recovery path are not done. T003: a Windows probe exists in experiments/windows-layered and compiles for the Windows target, but has never been run; it answers nothing until someone watches it on a real screen. T004: a macOS probe exists in experiments/macos-overlay and compiles for the macOS target; nobody on the project has a Mac, so there is no route to running it.

T013: the toolbar is part of the Draw-mode surface, which accepts pointer input, so a control that looks interactive is one. A press on it never starts a gesture, the gaps between buttons belong to the toolbar, and buttons act on release over the same button. Hidden in PassThrough.

T015: pen and highlighter with per-tool colour, width and opacity; style captured at the press so a mid-gesture change cannot rewrite a stroke; samples thinned and bounded. T014 fixed whole-stroke opacity with pixel fixtures.

T016: line, arrow, rectangle and ellipse share one drag lifecycle and one style. A degenerate drag is discarded with a reason rather than stored. Arrowheads, outline shapes and drag-direction independence have pixel fixtures.
T017: swept-geometry hit testing over segments, not samples, with a tolerance that includes half the object width. Whole objects only. One sweep is one transaction.

T017: undo, redo and clear over inverse commands that restore position and style exactly. No-ops record nothing; a new edit truncates redo; history is bounded at 1,000 transactions and reports truncation.
T009: per-output documents with an output binding, recorded logical size, and an output-mismatch guard. Documents are independent. Output remapping on load is T021.
T009: output-local logical units throughout; width is in logical units. Actual scale, rotation, and the macOS flip are backend work (T018).

T002: capability vocabulary with Unknown/Available/NeedsUserAction/Unavailable and a doctor report exist. Only output_enumeration is observed as available on E001; every overlay capability remains unknown because no surface has been created.

T020/T021: versioned JSON, one session file. Loading validates fully before adopting anything, and an output mismatch is reported rather than the annotations being stretched or moved. No file picker yet.

T020: same-directory temporary file, flushed and synced, then renamed, so a failed save keeps the previous file. Size, schema, coordinates, width, opacity, shape variants and object counts are all validated before replacement.

T010: a mode change cancels an in-flight gesture, and a button held across a transition is ignored until released. Verified natively in E003 finding 5. T003: a Windows probe exists in experiments/windows-layered and compiles for the Windows target, but has never been run; it answers nothing until someone watches it on a real screen. T004: a macOS probe exists in experiments/macos-overlay and compiles for the macOS target; nobody on the project has a Mac, so there is no route to running it.
T010: transitions are numbered so stale callbacks are ignored; a failed transition withdraws before it reports. Native fault injection is T023.
T002: the doctor report exists and omits user content. Settings persistence and the shortcut recovery path are untouched (T012, T019).

Split on 2026-09-23: T036 covers selection, move, resize and delete, which are implemented. T028 covers text: Latin entry, rendering, move and resize are implemented as of 2026-09-24; IME, preedit, shaping and font fallback are not.
T014: the event loop blocks on sources rather than polling. Measured 0 CPU ticks over 10 idle seconds (E006).
T009: ink-core has no dependencies and 20 headless deterministic tests. The reducer is T010 and command history is T017.
T002: the six typed error classes exist and are covered by headless tests.

ADR-008. GNOME built and observed on the E001 machine (E017): zoom steps, drawing while zoomed, and restoring the user's settings on off, exit and after a kill. Windows (T038) and macOS (T039) report unknown.
